items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (crcWriter, genericShape, maxEncodedCells), but ~750 lines were added to shapeindex.go with few comments. The long encode/decode bodies explain little, and the magic `maxEdges = 10` default is repeated in two places without explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The project asked for a dedicated shapeindex_encode.go and per-shape methods next to each type. Instead everything was put in shapeindex.go. ShapeIndex.decode runs about 135 lines (1488-1622), over the 100-line cap. Unrelated rewrites of applyUpdatesInternal and makeIndexCell were bundled in.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every count read is bounded (maxEncodedShapes/Cells), allocations are chunked with min(n,1024), plus a CRC32 trailer and checks on IDs and cell order. Weaknesses: the magic defaults 10 and 1024 recur, encode silently skips nil shapes, and applyUpdatesInternal now silently rebuilds the whole cellMap.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Encode/Decode are additive and existing tags were not renumbered (new constants 6/7/8 sit below typeTagMinUser). But existing types changed behavior in passing: PointVector.ChainEdge, LaxLoop.ChainEdge, LaxPolygon.ChainPosition, and Polyline.decode's signature. Loop.typeTag() still returns None.
